description: External GPU end-to-end validation matrix for loading and quantization roadmap task 8. Entries are plans, not results.

Z-Image.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/z_image.yaml, entry z_image.default, whose tags include gfx950

Z-Image-Turbo.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/z_image_turbo.yaml, entry z_image_turbo.1gpu.rdna4, the only entries this model has. Steps, guidance and resolution describe the model rather than the accelerator, so they carry over to gfx950; guidance is 0.0 because the model is distilled and does not use classifier-free guidance.

FLUX.1-dev.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/flux.yaml, entry flux.usp, whose tags include gfx950

FLUX.2-dev.prompt: Cat astronaut raising a cat flag on the surface of moon
FLUX.2-dev.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/flux2.yaml, entry flux2.t2i_1k, whose tags include gfx950. Text-to-image rather than the image-to-image entries, since these cases pass no input image. The rdna4 entries run the same model at 4 steps, which is a throughput setting rather than this model's operating point.

FLUX.2-klein-9B.prompt: A spectacular sunset over the ocean
FLUX.2-klein-9B.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/flux2_klein.yaml, entry flux2_klein.default, whose tags include gfx950

FLUX.2-klein-4B.prompt: A spectacular sunset over the ocean
FLUX.2-klein-4B.source: xFuserFlux2Klein4BModel.default_input_values, inherited from the 9B runner: 2048x2048, 9 steps, guidance 1.0. Every entry in .ci/benchmark_configs/flux2_klein.yaml names the 9B checkpoint, so the 4B has no config of its own and the runner's own statement is used instead. That is 9 steps rather than the 4 the config asks of the 9B, which is a throughput setting for that checkpoint. The prompt is the family's, since a prompt is an input rather than an operating point and sharing it keeps the two klein models comparable.

Qwen-Image.prompt: A cat holding a sign that says hello world

FLUX.1-Kontext-dev.prompt: Add a cool hat to the cat
FLUX.1-Kontext-dev.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/flux_kontext.yaml, entry flux_kontext.default, whose tags include gfx950. The image this model edits is the one its own config passes, /app/data/flux_cat.png in the benchmark container, reached through XDIT_INPUT_IMAGE so a machine without that file reports an environment mismatch rather than a failure.

Qwen-Image-Edit.prompt: Add a cool hat to the cat.
Qwen-Image-Edit.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/qwen_image_edit.yaml, entry qwen_image_edit.default, and the same input image as the Kontext entry above, which is what that config passes.

HunyuanVideo.prompt: In the large cage, two puppies were wagging their tails at each other.
HunyuanVideo.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/hunyuanvideo.yaml, entry hunyuanvideo.default, whose tags include gfx950. Tiling and slicing come from that entry too: decoding 129 frames of 720p in one piece is a VAE memory cost the config declines to pay, and it is not a sampling choice.

Cosmos3-Nano.source: xFuserCosmos3SuperModel.default_input_values, which the Nano runner inherits: 720x1280, 189 frames, 35 steps, guidance 6.0. No benchmark config covers Cosmos3 at all, so the runner's own statement is the only operating point available. The prompt is the structured JSON the checkpoint ships as assets/example_t2v_prompt.json, with assets/negative_prompt.json as its negative, because this runner reads a .json prompt path and serializes it rather than taking prose: the model states that it expects JSON-formatted prompts, so a plain sentence would be the wrong input rather than a different one. Both files are byte-identical in the Nano and Super repos. They are reached through placeholders so a machine without the weights reports an environment mismatch instead of a failure.

Cosmos3-Super.source: xFuserCosmos3SuperModel.default_input_values: 720x1280, 189 frames, 35 steps, guidance 6.0, and the same shipped JSON prompt assets as the Nano entry above, for the reasons given there.

Wan2.1-I2V.prompt: Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside.
Wan2.1-I2V.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/wan2_1.yaml, entry wan2_1.default, whose tags include gfx950. Its input is /app/data/wan_input.jpg in the benchmark container, reached through the same XDIT_WAN_INPUT_IMAGE the curated Wan cases already use.

Wan2.2-I2V.prompt: Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside.
Wan2.2-I2V.source: .ci/benchmark_configs/wan2_2.yaml, entry wan2_2.default, whose tags include gfx950, except for guidance: that entry sets none, so the value is the 3.5 this runner declares in its own DefaultInputValues. The curated Wan2.2-I2V cases pass a shorter clip of their own and keep it, since a case's own arguments are applied after these.

Wan2.1-T2V.prompt: Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside.
Wan2.1-T2V.source: xFuserWan21T2VModel.default_input_values, since no benchmark config covers the text-to-video checkpoint: 720x1280, 81 frames, 40 steps, guidance 3.5. The prompt is the one the Wan2.1 image-to-video config uses, because a prompt is an input to the model rather than part of its operating point.

Wan2.2-T2V.prompt: Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside.
Wan2.2-T2V.source: xFuserWan22T2VModel.default_input_values, since the Wan2.2 config covers the image-to-video checkpoint only.

Wan2.2-TI2V.prompt: Summer beach vacation style, a white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard. The fluffy-furred feline gazes directly at the camera with a relaxed expression. Blurred beach scenery forms the background featuring crystal-clear waters, distant green hills, and a blue sky dotted with white clouds. The cat assumes a naturally relaxed posture, as if savoring the sea breeze and warm sunlight. A close-up shot highlights the feline's intricate details and the refreshing atmosphere of the seaside.
Wan2.2-TI2V.source: xFuserWan22TI2VModel.default_input_values, since no benchmark config covers the 5B text-and-image-to-video checkpoint: 736x1280, 121 frames, 50 steps, guidance 5.0. The task is required rather than chosen: this is the one runner serving two of them, valid_tasks=['i2v', 't2v'], and it rejects a run that names neither. i2v is the one that takes the input image the other Wan entries use; t2v refuses an image.

Krea-2-Raw.source: xFuserKrea2RawModel.default_input_values, since this model has no benchmark config at all: 2048x2048, 52 steps, guidance 3.5. The runner declares that operating point in code and its docstring repeats it, which is the model's own statement of how it is meant to run.

Krea-2-Turbo.source: xFuserKrea2TurboModel.default_input_values: 2048x2048 and the fixed 8-step CFG-free schedule the runner enforces, rejecting any other step count and overriding any guidance it is given.

Ideogram-4.prompt: A spectacular sunset over the ocean
Ideogram-4.source: xFuserIdeogram4Model.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. Guidance is null because the runner builds its own guidance schedule and only when it is given no value: any number here would replace the schedule the model ships with.

LingBot-Video-Dense.prompt: A white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard
LingBot-Video-Dense.source: xFuserLingBotVideoDenseModel.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. The runner supplies its own structured negative prompt, so no entry has to repeat it.

LingBot-Video-MoE.prompt: A white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard
LingBot-Video-MoE.source: xFuserLingBotVideoMoEModel.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. Same operating point as the dense runner it shares construction with, which declares the same values.

MiniMax-H3.prompt: A white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard
MiniMax-H3.source: xFuserMiniMaxH3Model.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. Guidance is null because the model is guidance-distilled and the runner forwards no guidance to the pipeline at all. The task is named because the runner declares four and refuses to pick one; t2va is the one that needs no input image.

MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA.prompt: A white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard
MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA.source: xFuserMiniMaxH3Ref2VAModel.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. Guidance is null for the same distillation reason as the base runner. ref2va is the only task this runner declares, and it takes a reference image, left as a placeholder so a machine without one is an environment mismatch rather than a broken load.

LTX-2.3.prompt: A white cat wearing sunglasses sits on a surfboard
LTX-2.3.source: xFuserLTX23VideoModel.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. The runner supplies its own negative prompt, so no entry has to repeat it.

Hunyuanvideo-1.5-Sparse.prompt: In the large cage, two puppies were wagging their tails
Hunyuanvideo-1.5-Sparse.source: xFuserHunyuanvideo15SparseModel.default_input_values, no benchmark config naming this model. Guidance is null because the 1.5 runner forwards no guidance to the pipeline. The sparse runner declares i2v as its only task, so an image is named as a placeholder.

cases.quality_notes: Compare text fidelity and composition against the bf16 case with the same seed.
Confirm the logged Transformers 4 text-encoder fallback is post-load, then compare to the Transformers 5 result.
Verify peer ranks do not independently retain a full host copy of replicated weights.

Inspect both transformer phases; transformer_2 is expected to remain FP8. Unrun, and the success expectation needs checking against the MXFP4 FSDP2 gate: the FP4 half targets transformer.blocks, which the strategy also wraps, so validate_format_fsdp_placement is required and refuses unless torch carries pytorch/pytorch#177948 (2.12). On an older torch expect a preflight_failure instead.
The Qwen3VL text encoder is excluded from quantization; record host transfer behavior.
Compare first/last FP8 override ranges to an all-FP8 reference.
Expected rejection must occur before checkpoint allocation.
Expected rejection must precede reads of the external LightX2V state dicts.
The composition adapter has no standard meta-construction seam.
The manual single-file fallback is intentionally excluded from collective loading.
FSDP cannot safely apply the Transformers 4 text-encoder post-load fallback.
Record the pinned refs/pr/18 transformer load and blockwise fill.
Confirm TorchAO is selected instead of AITER block-scale FP8.
Check native TorchAO text-encoder loading and rank-to-rank output determinism.

Narrowed from non_rdna4_rocm to gfx942: _AITER_FP4_UNSUPPORTED_ARCHS names only gfx942, so this rejection is that arch's behaviour rather than all of non-RDNA4 ROCm. gfx950 accepts FP4 and is covered by rocm-gfx950-flux2-fp4-eager. FLUX.2-dev is a gated repo, so a run needs hub auth; a 401 previously matched the rejection pattern and was mis-scored.

First FP4 success expected on ROCm outside RDNA4. probe_format_backend_capabilities on gfx950 reports aiter_mxfp4 available with no reason, where gfx942 refuses it because AITER compiles no Float4_e2m1fn_x2 kernels for that arch. Predicted from the probe; not yet run.

Replicated meta load does not shard, so the packed MXFP4 weight never reaches FSDP2 and the torch limitation that blocks the fsdp_blockwise case does not apply. Text encoder stays unquantized by declaration.

Still rejected on gfx950, but for the torch version rather than the architecture: MXFP4 packs two 4-bit values into a uint8, and FSDP2 before pytorch/pytorch#177948 (torch 2.12) cannot shard a non-floating-point parameter. This image carries 2.9.1. Krea-2 quantizes transformer.transformer_blocks and wraps the same blocks for FSDP, so the placement check is required and fires. Expect this case to flip to inference_success on a torch 2.12 image.
ROCm INT8 must reject before model allocation.
Compare transformer-only and text-encoder FP8 quality using the same prompt and seed.
Verify minimum-size exclusions and context_refiner exclusion under sequence parallelism.
NVFP4 requires CUDA capability 10.0 or newer.
Verify both transformer components fill and execute under FSDP.
Record transfer overhead and compare output to the non-offloaded INT8 case.
Use a fixed source image and retain it with the result bundle.
Validate the shared transformer construction seam with stage-2 LoRA application.
The LoRA-before-fill ordering is not valid for the FSDP meta path.
Confirm native Diffusers NVFP4 streaming and compare against bf16 and FP8 references.
Text encoder remains unquantized by declaration.

Record whether installed TorchAO tensor subclasses satisfy composable FSDP hooks. Unrun, and as written the code cannot satisfy it: _probe_fsdp_support returns a hardcoded false for nvfp4 with "NVFP4 tensor-subclass FSDP gather/scatter support is not validated", so this rejects on any Blackwell box until that probe is implemented. Keep it as the target, but expect a preflight_failure today.
CUDA NVFP4 has no runtime FP8/FP4 hybrid wrapper.
Record host and device peaks while group offload streams quantized components.
Run with a pre-populated HF_HOME and network disabled; retain the resolved snapshot revision.
Unquantized reference for every other case in this file.
Confirm TorchAO FP8 is selected on gfx942, not AITER block-scale (RDNA4-only).
Native TorchAO text-encoder streaming for the UMT5 encoder; watch for text-conditioning loss.
Memory-efficient FSDP blockwise meta-load across both Wan2.2 transformers; compare peak VRAM against the eager FP8 case.
Control for the ulysses=4 replicated case; the RoPE buffer-dtype corruption survived ulysses<=2.
Rank0 broadcast load at the sequence-parallel degree where buffer-dtype corruption previously produced black output. Inspect the video, not just the exit status.

Same parallel degree as the replicated case but with the ordinary N-rank load, so a pixel diff against mi300x-wan22-i2v-fp8-replicated4 isolates the memory-efficient load from sequence-parallel attention numerics.
Unquantized ulysses-4 reference. Paired with mi300x-wan22-i2v-bf16-replicated4 this isolates the memory-efficient load itself: with no quantization in the way, the two must agree bit for bit.
Rank0 broadcast load with no quantization. Any pixel difference against the eager ulysses-4 control is attributable to the load path alone.
AITER compiles no FP4 kernels for gfx942, so this must be rejected in preflight. Before the gate landed it reached AITER_CHECK(false) after a full model load and died on SIGABRT.
Rejected twice over on this node: no AITER FP4 kernels for gfx942, and torch 2.9.1 FSDP2 cannot shard the uint8 MXFP4 packed parameter. The arch gate fires first.
Unquantized reference for the klein-4B memory-efficient cases; compare composition and text fidelity against them at the same seed.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserIdeogram4Model does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*single-file state dict

cases.quality_notes: The withheld reason has to be raised before allocation, not discovered as a wrong-weights image: this runner applies a single-file state dict outside the transformer seam and loads a second denoiser from its own subfolder.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserLingBotVideoDenseModel does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*composed _build_pipe

cases.quality_notes: Shares the MoE runner's composed construction and LingBot's own per-block wrapping, so the dense checkpoint must be refused for the same reason and say so.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserLingBotVideoMoEModel does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*fp32 norm and router

cases.quality_notes: The reason names the minority-dtype fp32 norm and router parameters that LingBot's own wrapping leaves unsharded, which xDiT's sharding path would shard instead.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserMiniMaxH3Model does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*fuse_qkv_projections

cases.quality_notes: Refusing before allocation is what keeps a 330G checkpoint from being read only to find that qkv fusion has renamed the tensors the shards would be filled from.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserMiniMaxH3Ref2VAModel does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*transformer_ref

cases.quality_notes: The reference workflow loads its denoiser as transformer_ref, so its refusal is a separate assertion from the base runner's rather than an inherited one.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserLTX23VideoModel does not support fsdp_meta materialization.*LoRA is applied before

cases.quality_notes: Applying the stage 2 distilled LoRA before the base checkpoint reaches a meta transformer is a load order, not a capability, so the refusal names the order that has to change.

expected.error_pattern: xFuserHunyuanvideo15SparseModel does not support replicated_meta materialization.*sparse blocks outside _build_transformer

cases.quality_notes: Composing base non-block weights with remapped Tencent sparse blocks happens outside the transformer seam, so the refusal has to come from the preflight rather than from the composition failing later. Replicated rather than sharded because the sharded flag never reaches the load declaration for this family: the capability gate refuses it first, which rocm-hunyuan15-sparse-fsdp-flag-refused pins separately. A sparse attention backend is named because this runner refuses to run without one, which would otherwise be the failure this case recorded.

The HunyuanVideo 1.5 runners declare no fully_shard_degree capability at all, so the sharding flag is refused while the config is validated, before any load contract is selected. Asserted separately from the withheld reason because it is an earlier and stronger refusal: it holds however the load declaration later changes.
